feat.title: Features
page.keys.sub: The keys Figghost listens to, in one place. Click a shortcut, then press the new keys.
keys.sec.panel: In the notch and the clipboard popup
keys.board.title: Put in the next board
keys.board.desc: Boards group pinned items above the clipboard list.
keys.pastealt.desc: Keeps the formatting when pasting without it is on, and the other way round.
keys.delete.title: Delete, deny or dismiss
keys.delete.desc: Deletes the selected item, refuses what an agent asks and dismisses a calendar alert.
keys.fixed.desc: They work as they do everywhere on the Mac and stay as they are.
keys.fixed.tab: Switch tab or paste a row
keys.elsewhere: Several shortcuts, set on its own page.
target.keys:paste_other: the key that pastes the other way
fault.reserved: Command with one key already means a tab, a pinned item or Delete in the panels. Add Option, Control or Shift.
page.scroll.sub: Smooth, reversible mouse-wheel scrolling. Trackpads and the Magic Mouse are never touched.
page.clipboard.sub: A history of everything you copy, with instant search, pinning and keyboard shortcuts.
page.notch.sub: A panel that grows out of the top edge of your screen. Closed, it shows what is playing and what your coding agents do; under the pointer it opens into your tabs.
page.agents.sub: Follow Claude Code and Codex from the notch: answer their permission requests, see what they are doing and how much of your limits is left.
agents.enable.title: Follow coding agents
agents.enable.desc: Listen for what Claude Code and Codex report and show it on the Agents tab of the notch.
agents.claude.title: Claude Code
agents.claude.desc: Adds hooks to ~/.claude/settings.json. Your other hooks stay as they are.
agents.codex.title: Codex
agents.codex.desc: Adds hooks to ~/.codex/hooks.json. Codex asks you to review new hooks the first time it runs.
agents.agy.title: Antigravity
agents.agy.desc: Adds a hook named figghost to ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, next to your own. The agy command line tool then shows its sessions on the notch, working, finished or failed. It asks for permissions in its own terminal as before.
agents.pi.title: Pi
agents.pi.desc: Adds an extension to ~/.pi/agent/extensions/figghost.ts. Pi loads it the next time it starts; its questions can then be answered on the notch as well as in its terminal.
agents.wait.title: Wait for an answer
agents.wait.desc: A command waits this long on the notch. Without an answer the agent asks in its own terminal, as usual.
agents.sound.title: Play a sound
agents.sound.desc: When a command needs an answer or an agent finishes.
agents.peek.title: Say so in the notch when an agent finishes
agents.peek.desc: The closed notch shows it for a few seconds; it does not open.
agents.usage.title: Claude Code limits
agents.usage.desc: Claude Code reports how much of its five-hour and weekly limits is used to its status line. Turning this on runs Figghost there first and then your own status line, so it looks the same. Codex limits are read from its session logs and need nothing. The refresh button on the Agents tab also asks the Codex program installed on this Mac for its current limits: Codex contacts OpenAI itself, as it does whenever you use it, and Figghost sends nothing and never reads the Codex login.
agents.usage.waiting: Waiting for the next message from Claude Code.
agents.note.title: Other apps that answer permission requests
agents.note.body: If another app, such as OneNotch, also answers these requests, both ask and the first answer wins. Turn one of them off.
tab.agents.desc: Claude Code and Codex: the command waiting for you, the sessions that are running and what is left of their limits.
tab.calendar.desc: Today and tomorrow, the reminders that are due, and an alert with a Join button before a meeting. Off until you turn it on in the Calendar page.
fault.agents_failed: Could not change the agent files.
page.tiling.sub: Place the focused window on a part of the screen with a shortcut.
page.about.sub: One light app for the small tools of a Mac.
hero.tagline: Smooth scrolling, clipboard history and a notch toolbox in one quiet menu bar app.
login.title: Launch at login
login.desc: Start Figghost when you log in. The window stays closed; use the menu bar icon.
login.approval: Allow Figghost in System Settings, under Login Items, to finish.
login.unavailable: Available when Figghost runs as an app from a folder such as Applications.
showlaunch.title: Open this window at start
showlaunch.desc: Show settings each time you open the app yourself. Never at login.
hello.title: Say hello at start
hello.desc: Each time you open Figghost yourself, its ghost comes out of the notch and blinks. Never at login or in the background, and only while the notch is on.
lang.title: Language
lang.desc: This window changes at once. Menus and the notch change after a restart.
lang.restart: Restart Figghost to use the new language in menus and the notch.
access.title: Accessibility
access.desc: Needed for smooth scrolling, pasting into other apps, window snapping and the volume indicator.
perm.all_desc: Check and grant all system permissions Figghost uses.
data.title: Settings folder
data.desc: Where your settings, clipboard history and shelf are stored. Everything stays on this Mac.
smooth.title: Smooth scrolling
smooth.desc: Turns each wheel notch into a gliding motion.
reverse.title: Reverse wheel direction
reverse.desc: Only mouse wheels are reversed. The trackpad keeps its natural direction.
step.title: Step
speed.title: Speed
duration.title: Glide
duration.desc: How long a glide takes to settle
pad.hint: Scroll here with your mouse wheel to feel the settings.
shift.title: Shift scrolls sideways
shift.desc: Hold Shift and turn the wheel to scroll horizontally, smoothly.
option.title: Option scrolls faster
option.desc: Hold Option to scroll several times as far. Good for long documents.
boost.title: Boost
cmd.title: Command zooms
cmd.desc: Hold Command and turn the wheel to zoom in or out. Sends Command + and Command - in browsers, editors and viewers.
apps.desc: With Smooth scrolling on, set an app to Off to leave it alone (a block list). With it off, set an app to On and only those apps glide (an allow list).
clip.hotkey.title: Open clipboard history
clip.hotkey.desc: Works everywhere. The popup appears next to the pointer.
paste.auto.title: Paste automatically
paste.auto.desc: Press Enter on an item to paste it into the app you were using. Off copies only.
paste.plain.title: Paste without formatting
paste.plain.desc: Text goes in as plain text. {key} does the opposite for one paste.
limit.title: Items to keep
count.title: In the history now
clear.title: Clear history
clear.desc: Removes every item that is not pinned.
clear.confirm.title: Clear the clipboard history?
clear.confirm.body: Every item that is not pinned is removed. This cannot be undone.
ignored.title: Never record copies from
ignored.desc: Password managers and items marked as concealed are always skipped.
notch.panel.title: Notch panel
notch.panel.desc: Move the pointer to the top edge of the screen to open it. Off removes it entirely.
notch.preview: Hover or press to open the notch
tab.waiting: Not in the notch yet: its tab appears when its feature is turned on, on its page.
tab.clipboard.desc: The same list as the popup, with search.
tab.shelf.desc: Drop files to keep them handy and drag them out again. Right-click a file to compress it or convert an image. Only references are stored.
tab.media.desc: Previous, play and next for whatever plays, browsers included, with its cover, the app it comes from and the time.
vol.title: Volume indicator in the notch
vol.desc: Replaces the system volume display. Needs Accessibility. Shift + Option moves in finer steps.
vol.style.title: Indicator style
vol.style.desc: How the volume panel looks while the keys are pressed.
vol.style.glass.desc: The same hang, in Liquid Glass.
vol.style.bar.desc: The level fills the notch shape.
vol.style.ring.desc: A round glass dial with a ring.
vol.style.equalizer.desc: Bars that light up as it grows.
vol.place.title: Where it shows
vol.place.desc: For the floating styles; the ones that hang stay under the notch.
vol.preview.title: Try it
vol.preview.desc: Shows the indicator now with the style and place you chose.
shelf.clear.desc: Removes the references only. Your files are not touched.
tiling.enable.title: Window snapping
tiling.enable.desc: Move and resize the focused window with a shortcut. Command+1–9 are global and may replace shortcuts in other apps. Needs Accessibility.
about.line: A light native toolbox for the menu bar and the notch of your Mac.
about.usage.title: What Figghost is using
about.usage.desc: Read every two seconds while this window is open. The network counts the tools Figghost runs, such as curl and gh, since the app opens no connection of its own. Frames are those its animations draw: none while nothing moves.
about.privacy.val: Everything stays on this Mac. The only thing Figghost asks the network by itself is whether a new version exists, once a day.
about.quit.desc: Stops scrolling, clipboard and notch features until you open the app again.
about.update.desc: Looks for a new version every day. Press Check now to look at once; a new version is downloaded and installed for you.
about.update.ready: Version {v} is installed. Restart Figghost to use it.
about.update.blocked: Version {v} is out, but it could not be installed here: {detail}
update.news.title: What's new after an update
update.news.desc: Opens a short tour of the new features the first time a new version runs. Many changes show as slides.
update.auto.title: Update automatically
update.auto.desc: Install a new version as soon as it is found, without asking. Otherwise Figghost asks once a day. Either way, restart Figghost to use it.
fault.needs_modifier: Add Control, Option, Shift or Command.
fault.taken: Another app already uses this shortcut.
fault.accessibility_needed: Accessibility access is needed. Allow Figghost in System Settings.
fault.login_failed: Could not change the login item: {detail}
mcp.title: Let AI assistants search the history
mcp.desc: Starts a local server (MCP) that Claude and other assistants can use to find what you copied. Anything in the history can be read while this is on.
mcp.how: Add this to the assistant's MCP settings:
notch.hover.title: Open on hover
notch.hover.desc: Move the pointer onto the notch to open it. Off: a click opens it.
notch.delay.title: Hover delay
notch.delay.desc: How long the pointer rests on the notch before it opens. A longer delay keeps it shut when the pointer only passes by.
notch.width.title: Width
notch.width.desc: How wide the open notch is. Automatic fits each tab; a wider notch keeps the tab in the middle.
notch.style.reset.title: Back to standard
notch.height.title: Height
notch.height.desc: How tall the open notch is. Automatic fits each tab; a taller notch leaves room below it.
notch.restwidth.title: Closed width
notch.restwidth.desc: How wide the closed notch is on a screen without a hardware notch. A real notch keeps its own size.
notch.restheight.title: Closed height
notch.restheight.desc: How tall the closed notch is on a screen without a hardware notch.
notch.openpage.title: Opens on
notch.openpage.desc: The tab shown when the notch opens.
notch.haptics.title: Haptic feedback
notch.haptics.desc: A light tap on a Force Touch trackpad when the notch opens under the pointer.
notch.shortcut.title: Open or close the notch
notch.shortcut.desc: A shortcut that works everywhere. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
notch.material.title: Material
notch.material.desc: Liquid Glass lets the desktop show through and bends it at the edges. Closed, the notch stays black, like a hardware notch.
notch.motion.title: Motion
notch.motion.desc: How the notch moves as it opens, closes and widens. Reduce Motion in System Settings turns movement off.
notch.shadow.title: Shadow
notch.shadow.desc: A soft shadow under the open notch.
notch.display.title: Show on
notch.display.desc: The screen the notch lives on.
notch.rest.title: On a screen without a notch
notch.rest.desc: A black tab where a notch would be, or nothing until the pointer reaches the top edge.
notch.rest.hardware: This screen has a notch of its own.
notch.cutout.title: Camera cutout
notch.cutout.desc: Where a notification goes on the closed notch: below the camera of a screen with a cutout, or from the top edge.
notch.restclock.title: Date and time
notch.restclock.desc: Shows the weekday, date and time in the closed notch, as much of them as fits: across the pill, or in the two ears of a hardware notch. While it is on, the pill stays on screen even when the setting above is Hidden.
notch.reststeps.title: Previous and next buttons
notch.reststeps.desc: Two buttons beside the date and time: they skip to the previous or next track while music plays, and otherwise open the previous or next tab.
notch.capture.title: Hide in screenshots and recordings
notch.capture.desc: The notch stays out of every screenshot and screen recording, including this app's own.
notch.fullscreen.title: Show over full-screen apps
notch.fullscreen.desc: Off hides the notch completely while the app in front is full screen on its screen, and brings it back when that app leaves full screen.
tabs.desc: Turn tabs on or off and change their order. Command + 1 to 9 follow this order.
tab.sound.desc: Volume, output and equalizer for each app that plays.
notch.livemedia.title: Music in the closed notch
notch.livemedia.desc: While something plays, in any app or browser, the closed notch shows its cover and moving bars. Point at it to open the player.
notch.waveform.title: Bars
notch.waveform.desc: Follow the sound the Mac plays (macOS asks once for System Audio Recording; nothing is recorded), or only move.
notch.liveagents.title: Coding agents in the closed notch
notch.liveagents.desc: While Claude Code or Codex works, the closed notch shows it with the share of the five-hour limit used. A question waits there too.
menuicon.title: Show the icon in the menu bar
menuicon.desc: Without it, open Figghost again from Finder or Spotlight to reach these settings.
theme.title: Settings window
theme.desc: Light, dark, or as the system is.
agents.ask.title: Open the notch for a question
agents.ask.desc: Off: a question waits in the closed notch, breathing, until you point at it. On: the notch opens by itself.
agents.tokens.title: Count tokens and cost
agents.tokens.desc: Read from the transcripts Claude Code and Codex keep on this Mac; nothing is sent anywhere. The cost is what the same work would cost at Anthropic's API list prices. A subscription is billed a flat fee, so it is not a charge.
agents.spend.none: Nothing counted yet. The numbers appear once Claude Code or Codex has run on this Mac.
adv.title: {page}: advanced
page.volume.sub: A volume indicator in the notch, in place of the one of the system.
page.menubar.sub: Hides the menu bar icons you rarely need behind an arrow.
page.shelf.sub: Files dropped on the notch, kept there for a while.
page.media.sub: What plays, on a tab of the notch.
accounts.intro.title: Accounts in Orca
accounts.intro.body: The Claude Code and Codex accounts you keep in Orca. Switching to one copies its sign-in to the plain claude (or codex) command, after keeping a private copy of the account the command used, which Restore puts back.
accounts.cli.outside: The claude command uses {email}, an account Orca does not keep. A switch keeps a copy of it, so Restore brings it back.
accounts.switch.title: Use {email} for the {cmd} command?
accounts.switch.body.claude: Figghost keeps a private copy of the account the command uses now, so Restore can bring it back. New Claude Code sessions use the new account; running ones may need a restart. The account then shares one sign-in with Orca: when one of them renews it, the other may have to sign in again.
accounts.switch.body.codex: Figghost keeps a private copy of ~/.codex/auth.json, so Restore can bring it back. New Codex sessions use the new account; running ones may need a restart.
accounts.refresh.title: Limits of each account
accounts.limits.desc: Refresh asks Anthropic for the limits of each Claude account with its own sign-in, read from the Keychain; macOS asks you first whether Figghost may read it. After that they are asked again every five minutes while this page is open. A sign-in that has run out is never renewed here, because that would sign Orca out; its numbers come back once Orca or Claude Code has renewed it.
accounts.nokeychain: A private instance does not use the Keychain.
accounts.note.none: Press Refresh to see the limits.
accounts.note.expired: The sign-in has run out. The numbers come back once Orca or Claude Code renews it.
accounts.note.no_sign_in: No sign-in was found for this account. Sign in to it again in Orca.
accounts.note.refused: The Keychain did not let Figghost read the sign-in. Press Refresh to be asked again.
accounts.note.failed: Anthropic did not give the limits. Try again later.
accounts.note.codex: The limits of Codex accounts are not shown here.
accounts.empty: Orca keeps no Claude Code or Codex accounts on this Mac.
accounts.restore.claude: Restore the previous Claude Code account
accounts.restore.desc: Puts back the sign-in the command had before the last switch.
accounts.done.switched: Switched. New sessions use the new account.
about.what.title: One light app for the small tools of a Mac
about.what.body: Smooth mouse-wheel scrolling and a pointer of your own, a clipboard history, window snapping from the notch, and a panel that grows out of the notch with tabs for files, media, your calendar, coding agents, weather, system health and more. Vietnamese typing in every app, Smart Select, Translate, screenshots, screen recordings, a colour picker, sound for each app and a window kept on top can be switched on when you want them.
about.native.title: Native, and kept on this Mac
about.native.body: It is written in Rust on AppKit, with no browser engine in the app itself; only this settings window is a web page. It idles light, comes in English and Vietnamese, and everything it keeps stays on this Mac.
about.why.title: Why it exists
about.why.body: Smooth scrolling, a clipboard history and a notch toolbox usually come as separate apps: Mos, Maccy and OneNotch gave it its ideas, SoundSource and CleanShot X those of the sound and capture tools, and Gõ Nhanh the engine of its Vietnamese typing, used unchanged. Figghost brings them into one app with one permission prompt, one login item and one settings window. Their ideas inspired it; its code and artwork are its own.
about.versions.title: Versions
about.v.0_2.body: Sound for each app, screenshots, scrolling capture and screen recordings with an editor, the settings window, AI agents on the notch, Smart Select, a calendar, lyrics, snapping to the notch, a menu bar icon hider and Copy Stack.
about.v.0_4.body: Every surface rebuilt on Liquid Glass, and the clipboard mascot.
about.v.0_5.body: Mole: the health, clean-up and uninstall tools of the Mac on a page of their own.
about.v.0_6.body: Updating from inside the app: a daily look for a new version, the download and the install, with what is new shown first.
about.v.0_7.body: A redesigned notch, and the Drag wheel, which converts files and runs tools on them while you drag.
about.v.0_8.body: A new app icon and a sidebar with a name beside every icon.
about.v.0_9.body: A hello from the ghost, Translate, Bluetooth in the notch, 3D sound, and window snapping in two steps with layouts of your own.
about.v.1_0.body: The first big release: a custom cursor, Always on top, a Shortcuts page, a search field for the settings, and a simpler area picker for screenshots.
about.v.1_x.body: Questions answered on the notch, a music widget and more volume indicators, a permissions check, ten more notch tabs (System, Notes, Launcher, Weather, Pull requests, Pomodoro, Screen Time, Day progress, Devices and Displays), live islands, utilities, Orca accounts, pi, and Vietnamese typing.
about.v.2_0.body: A new settings window on Liquid Glass: the page groups are icons in a floating dock with a lens you can drag, and the search is in the title bar.
about.v.2_0_2.body: The language of Vietnamese typing on the notch and in the menu bar, a shortcut that can be recorded even when the system uses it, Spotlight, and a dock with clearer icons.

page.smart.sub: Select text anywhere and press the shortcut to see it converted: units, money and times, and a translation of other text.
smart.enable.title: Use Smart Select
smart.enable.desc: It reads the selected text only when you press the shortcut or choose it from the menu bar item.
smart.shortcut.title: Shortcut
smart.shortcut.desc: Works in any app. Return copies the highlighted answer and Escape closes the window.
smart.access.title: Reading the selection
smart.access.desc: Needs Accessibility access. An app that does not share its selection is read by copying it for a moment: your clipboard is put back as it was and the history does not record it.
smart.try.title: Try it
smart.try.desc: Shows the answers for "5 km" next to the pointer, without selecting anything.
smart.net.title: Use the internet
smart.net.desc: Converts money with the exchange rates of the day and translates other text. The rates are downloaded from open.er-api.com and nothing about you or your text is sent. Translating sends the selected text to api.mymemory.translated.net. Off by default.
smart.lang.title: Translate into
smart.lang.desc: The language that translations go into.
smart.rates.title: Exchange rates
smart.cur.title: Currencies
smart.cur.desc: Amounts are converted into these. Three-letter codes separated by spaces, up to six.
smart.cur.label: Currencies
smart.zones.title: Time zones
smart.zones.desc: A time such as 3pm PST is also shown in your own zone and in these. Names like Asia/Tokyo or UTC separated by spaces, up to six.
smart.zones.label: Time zones
smart.k.units.desc: Length, weight, volume, area, speed, temperature and data size, between metric and imperial.
smart.k.money.desc: Amounts such as $100, 50 EUR or 5tr d, in the currencies above.
smart.k.time.desc: Times such as 3pm PST, 15:30 UTC+7 or 9am in Tokyo.
smart.k.words.desc: Any other text is translated when the internet is on.
page.translate.sub: Select text anywhere and press the shortcut: a glass window next to the pointer translates it into the language you choose.
translate.enable.title: Use Translate
translate.enable.desc: The selected text is read only when you press the shortcut or choose Translate from the menu bar item. It is sent to api.mymemory.translated.net to be translated, which is the only thing sent.
translate.shortcut.title: Shortcut
translate.shortcut.desc: Works in any app. Return or a click copies the translation and Escape closes the window.
translate.access.title: Reading the selection
translate.access.desc: Needs Accessibility access. An app that does not share its selection is read by copying it for a moment: your clipboard is put back as it was and the history does not record it.
translate.try.title: Try it
translate.try.desc: Translates a sample sentence next to the pointer, without selecting anything.
translate.style.title: Window style
translate.style.desc: The glass the translation window is made of.
translate.lang.title: Translate into
translate.lang.desc: The language that translations go into. The language of the text is detected for you. Up to 450 characters at a time.
page.rewrite.sub: Select text anywhere and press the shortcut: a glass window next to the pointer shows it fixed, more formal, shorter or in English.
rewrite.enable.title: Use Rewrite
rewrite.enable.desc: The selected text is read only when you press the shortcut or choose Rewrite from the menu bar item. It is sent, over https, to the model that Jarvis is set to ask (its own service, or the model on this Mac): set the provider and its key on the Jarvis page. Nothing else is sent and nothing is kept.
rewrite.model.title: The model
rewrite.model.ready: Jarvis is ready to be asked.
rewrite.shortcut.title: Shortcut
rewrite.shortcut.desc: Works in any app. Return uses the result and Escape closes the window.
rewrite.access.title: Reading the selection
rewrite.access.desc: Needs Accessibility access. An app that does not share its selection is read by copying it for a moment: your clipboard is put back as it was and the history does not record it.
rewrite.try.title: Try it
rewrite.try.desc: Rewrites a sample sentence with its mistakes, without selecting anything.
rewrite.mode.title: Rewrite as
rewrite.mode.desc: What the shortcut asks of the model. Up to 4000 characters at a time.
rewrite.replace.title: Replace the selection
rewrite.replace.desc: Return pastes the result over what you selected, with Command+V, and puts your clipboard back. Needs Accessibility; without it the result is copied. Off, Return only copies it.
rewrite.style.title: Window style
rewrite.style.desc: The glass the window is made of.
page.palette.sub: One shortcut, then type: open a tab or a page, turn a feature on or off, go to the agent that waits, test a connection, add a reminder.
palette.enable.title: Use the command palette
palette.enable.desc: Opens a small window with a field to type in. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is kept.
palette.shortcut.title: Shortcut
palette.shortcut.desc: Works in any app. Press it again, or Escape, to close the window.
palette.links.title: figghost:// addresses
palette.links.desc: Shortcuts, scripts and links can open Figghost with an address. Only these do anything, and none changes a setting or sends data: figghost://palette, figghost://page/network, figghost://tab/pomodoro, figghost://agents/jump and figghost://remind?text=call%20mom%20tomorrow%209h.
palette.jump: Go to the agent that waits longest
palette.jump.hint: Brings its terminal to the front
palette.export: Export the network history of 7 days as CSV
palette.remind.hint: Say when too: tomorrow 9h, friday 5pm, in 30 minutes
page.mirror.sub: See yourself before a call, and read a script near the camera while you talk to it.
mirror.enable.title: Use the mirror and the teleprompter
mirror.enable.desc: The camera is opened only while the mirror shows, and what it sees is drawn on the screen and kept nowhere. The teleprompter reads the note you wrote last in the Notes tab and sends nothing anywhere.
mirror.shortcut.title: Mirror shortcut
mirror.shortcut.desc: Shows the camera, mirrored, under the notch; drag it where you like. Press it again to close.
mirror.size.title: Size
mirror.size.desc: The mirror is a square of this many points.
mirror.camera.title: Camera access
mirror.camera.desc: The mirror needs access to the camera. The first time it is asked for, macOS asks you.
mirror.prompter.shortcut.title: Teleprompter shortcut
mirror.prompter.shortcut.desc: Starts and stops the strip under the menu bar. While it runs, Control, Option and Command with Space pause it, with Up and Down speed it up and slow it down, and with Left start it again.
mirror.note.title: The script
mirror.note.desc: It reads the note written last in the Notes tab, so write or paste your script there first.
mirror.note.none: There is no note to read yet.
mirror.text.title: Letters
mirror.text.desc: The size of the text, in points.
mirror.speed.title: Speed
mirror.speed.desc: How fast the text rises: 1 is slow, 6 is fast.
mirror.hide.title: Keep it out of recordings
mirror.hide.desc: Screenshots, recordings and screen sharing leave the strip out, so that the people you talk to do not see your script. Some apps may still capture it.
page.commands.sub: Save a few commands, then run them from a tab of the notch and watch what they print.
commands.enable.title: Show the Commands tab
commands.enable.desc: A tab of the notch with the commands below. Each runs when pressed, with your shell (zsh) from your home folder, and what it prints scrolls in the tab. It is a runner and not a terminal: a command gets no keyboard and no screen to draw on, one runs at a time, and one that runs for over ten minutes is stopped. Nothing it prints is kept.
commands.items.desc: A name, and the line to run, such as cd ~/project && npm test. The line runs exactly as written, as you: only put in what you would type in Terminal.
commands.name: Name
commands.bad: Every command needs a name and a line, each of plain text on one line. Nothing is saved until they do.
page.capture.sub: Areas, windows and displays, text, long pages, and videos or GIFs of the screen.
capture.enable.title: Screenshots and recordings
capture.enable.desc: The shortcuts below and the Capture menu of the menu bar item.
capture.access.title: Screen Recording access
capture.access.no: Needed for every capture. Allow Figghost in System Settings, then capture again.
capture.save.title: Save to the folder
capture.save.desc: Off keeps captures in a temporary folder, for the quick panel only.
capture.folder.title: Folder
capture.copy.title: Copy
capture.copy.desc: Pictures go to the clipboard as images, recordings as files.
capture.quick.title: Quick panel
capture.quick.desc: A thumbnail in the corner with Copy, Save, Edit and Pin. Drag it into another app to drop the file there.
capture.quick_seconds.title: The quick panel stays
capture.timer.title: Countdown of a timed capture
capture.kind.text: Copy the text of an area
capture.kind.record: Record the screen, again to stop
capture.kind.gif: Record a GIF, again to stop
capture.kind.again: Capture again, the same kind as the last one
capture.kind.folder: Open the folder of the captures
capture.record.system_audio.title: Computer audio
capture.record.system_audio.desc: What the apps play, as the Sound tab sets it.
capture.record.microphone.title: Microphone
capture.record.microphone.desc: macOS asks for access the first time.
capture.record.camera.title: Camera
capture.record.camera.desc: A round bubble in a corner of the recording; drag it to move it.
capture.record.clicks.title: Show clicks
capture.record.clicks.desc: A ring where the mouse is clicked.
capture.record.keys.title: Show shortcuts pressed
capture.record.keys.desc: Shortcuts and keys such as Return appear at the bottom. Plain typing never does, so passwords stay out.
page.vision.sub: Point at any pixel on the screen, see it magnified and copy its colour.
vision.enable.title: Colour picker
vision.enable.desc: A shortcut opens a loupe at the pointer. A click copies the colour, Tab changes the format and Esc cancels.
vision.shortcut.title: Shortcut
vision.shortcut.desc: Starts the picker from any app.
vision.format.title: Format
vision.format.desc: The format a pick starts in. Press Tab while picking to try the others.
vision.access.title: Screen Recording access
vision.access.desc: Reading the pixels of other apps needs this permission. After you allow it, macOS may ask to quit and reopen Figghost.
vision.bg.title: Remove background
vision.bg.desc: Right-click an image on the shelf and choose Remove background. A new PNG with a transparent background is made next to the original. Needs macOS 14 or later.
lyrics.show.title: Show lyrics
lyrics.show.desc: Shows the words of the song on the Media tab, line by line as it plays. Works with Music and Spotify.
lyrics.fetch.title: Fetch lyrics online
lyrics.fetch.desc: Looks lyrics up on lrclib.net, a free service. To do that it sends the artist, track and album names and the length of the track to lrclib.net, and nothing else. Lyrics that are found are kept on this Mac, so a song is asked about once; a song without lyrics is asked about again after a few days. With this off, only lyrics already kept are shown.
page.calendar.sub: Events, reminders and meeting alerts on the notch.
cal.enable.title: Calendar on the notch
cal.enable.desc: Shows today and tomorrow, reminders that are due, and opens the notch before a meeting.
cal.lead.title: Alert before a meeting
cal.lead.desc: The notch opens for a few seconds this long before an event starts.
cal.sound.title: Play a sound
cal.sound.desc: A short system sound with each alert.
cal.reminders.title: Include reminders
cal.reminders.desc: Reminders due by tomorrow or overdue, each with a button to complete it.
cal.allday.title: Include all-day events
cal.allday.desc: Holidays and birthdays are listed but never raise an alert.
cal.noprompt: This build has no permission text, so macOS cannot ask. Use the packaged app.
cal.calendars.empty: Turn the feature on and allow access to list your calendars.
cal.lists.empty: Turn on reminders and allow access to list your reminder lists.
cal.note.title: Stays on this Mac
cal.note.body: Events and reminders are read from the system and never sent anywhere. The only change Figghost makes is marking a reminder complete when you press its button. Meeting links open only for Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Webex, over https.
snap.enable.title: Snap by dragging to the notch
snap.enable.desc: Drag a window by its title bar to the top edge of the screen. The layouts appear under the notch. Point at one to see its cells on the screen, then move down into a cell and release to put the window there. Releasing anywhere else changes nothing.
snap.access.title: Accessibility
snap.access.desc: Placing a window needs Accessibility access. Without it nothing happens when a window is dropped.
snap.screen.title: Layouts of a screen
snap.layouts.title: Layouts
snap.layouts.desc: Choose which layouts appear under the notch. Every screen can have a list of its own, and the others follow the list of all screens.
snap.screen.note.all: These layouts appear on every screen that has no list of its own.
snap.screen.note.own: This screen has a list of its own.
snap.screen.note.shared: This screen follows the list of all screens until you change a layout here.
snap.mine.title: Your layouts
snap.mine.desc: Divide the screen into a grid and join parts of it into larger cells. A layout you make can be chosen for any screen above.
snap.mine.none: No layouts of your own yet.
snap.edit.name: Name
snap.edit.name.needed: Type a name for the layout.
snap.edit.hint: Select two or more cells and press Join to make one larger cell. Select a joined cell and press Split to take it apart. Changing the columns or rows starts the grid again.
snap.delete.title: Delete this layout?
snap.delete.body: It is taken off the screens that offered it.
fault.snap_failed: Could not watch the mouse for window drags.
page.pin.sub: Press the shortcut and the window in front stays above all the others, with a red border round it. Press it again to let go.
pin.enable.title: Use Always on top
pin.enable.desc: One window is kept on top at a time, from the shortcut or from the switch in the menu bar panel. macOS lets a program raise only its own windows, so while another window covers the pinned one, Figghost shows a live picture of it over the cover. Click the picture and the real window comes forward.
pin.shortcut.title: Shortcut
pin.shortcut.desc: Keeps the window in front on top, or lets go of the one that is. Works in any app. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
pin.now.title: Window on top
pin.access.title: Accessibility
pin.access.desc: Finds the window in front, and brings the real window forward when you click its picture.
pin.screen.title: Screen Recording
pin.screen.desc: Takes the picture of the pinned window while it is covered. Pictures stay in memory; nothing is saved or sent. After you allow it, macOS may ask to quit and reopen Figghost.
page.cursor.sub: Give the pointer a look of its own: a rainbow arrow, a pixel character that blinks, or any picture or GIF you choose.
cursor.enable.title: Custom cursor
cursor.enable.desc: The arrow and the hand over links are drawn from the picture you choose below, and the system animates them, so nothing runs while the pointer moves. The text cursor stays as it is. The pointer goes back to normal when you turn this off or quit Figghost.
cursor.theme.title: Picture
cursor.theme.desc: A character stands and blinks, and beams when you point at a link.
cursor.custom.title: Your own picture
cursor.custom.desc: A GIF or an animated PNG plays as it is; any other picture stays still. Transparent backgrounds work.
cursor.custom.bad: This picture cannot be read. Choose another one.
cursor.tip.title: Point that clicks
cursor.tip.desc: Where on your picture the click lands.
cursor.size.title: Size
cursor.size.desc: How wide the pointer is, in points. The system arrow is about 17.
cursor.speed.title: Speed
cursor.note.title: Where it shows
cursor.note.desc: Over every other app. This window keeps the system pointer while it is in front, which is how macOS lets a program draw its own cursor, so look at another window to see the change.
page.musicwidget.sub: A player of Liquid Glass that floats on your desktop with the cover, the song and the controls of whatever plays. Drag it where you like and pull its corner to resize it.
musicwidget.enable.title: Show the music widget
musicwidget.enable.desc: Works with any player and with music in a browser. macOS lets no app draw on the lock screen, so the widget floats on every desktop instead, and over full-screen apps if you choose that below.
musicwidget.style.card.desc: The cover, the song, a bar and the buttons.
musicwidget.style.cover.desc: A big cover with the song over its foot.
musicwidget.style.vinyl.desc: A record that turns while it plays.
musicwidget.style.minimal.desc: Only the song and one button.
musicwidget.material.title: Material
musicwidget.material.desc: How much of the desktop shows through the glass.
musicwidget.ambient.title: Light from the cover
musicwidget.ambient.desc: A soft blur of the cover glows behind the controls and takes the colours of the music.
musicwidget.opacity.title: Opacity
musicwidget.opacity.desc: How solid the whole widget is.
musicwidget.layer.title: Stays
musicwidget.layer.desc: Where it floats, in front of or behind your windows.
musicwidget.hide_idle.title: Hide when nothing plays
musicwidget.hide_idle.desc: The widget goes away until music starts. Off keeps it on screen with a note.
musicwidget.width.title: Width
musicwidget.width.desc: You can also pull the corner of the widget.
musicwidget.height.title: Height
musicwidget.height.desc: The slim styles do not need much.
musicwidget.reset.title: Back to the start
musicwidget.reset.desc: Puts it at the foot of the screen at the size of its style.
menubar.enable.title: Hide menu bar icons
menubar.enable.desc: Adds an arrow and a divider to the menu bar. Icons to the left of the divider hide when you press the arrow. Off by default.
menubar.auto.title: Hide again by itself
menubar.auto.desc: How long the icons stay after you show them.
menubar.click.title: Show only when the arrow is clicked
menubar.click.desc: Off also shows the icons when the pointer rests on the arrow.
menubar.state.title: Right now
menubar.how.title: Choosing the icons to hide
menubar.how.body: Hold Command and drag an icon to the left of the divider (the thin line) to hide it, or to the right of it to keep it visible. A newly started app puts its icon at the far left, which is the hidden side: drag it over once. If the arrow ever ends up on the hidden side, "Show hidden menu bar icons" in the Fig menu still works.
menubar.limits.title: What this cannot do
menubar.limits.body: Icons that do not fit beside the notch are hidden by macOS itself and cannot be shown by this. On some macOS versions the longest divider that works depends on the display and on the app in front, so Figghost measures it and checks again after every change; where none works it leaves everything showing and says so here. Turning this off or quitting Figghost removes the arrow and the divider and every icon returns.
stack.copy.title: Copy Stack
stack.copy.desc: Double press a modifier key to start a stack. While it runs, every copy is queued and each Command+V pastes the next item in the order it was copied. It ends when the queue is empty or at another double press.
stack.key.title: Key to double press
stack.key.desc: Press it twice quickly, on its own. Used with another key, or held, it does nothing here.
stack.status.title: Status
stack.status.desc: Only Command+V is followed. Pasting from a menu or with another shortcut pastes what is on the clipboard.
stack.boards.title: Boards
stack.boards.desc: A board groups pinned items and shows as a chip above the clipboard list. {key} files the selected item in the next board, and a right click on a row offers a menu. Deleting a board keeps its items pinned.
stack.boards.name: Board name
stack.boards.confirm.title: Delete this board?
stack.boards.confirm.body: The items filed in it stay pinned and go back to the plain pinned list.
stack.sensitive.title: When a copy looks like a secret
stack.sensitive.desc: Card numbers, API keys and tokens, private keys and the value after a password or secret label are recognised. Copies from password managers and concealed copies are always left out, whatever you choose here.
stack.expire.title: Delete hidden items after
stack.expire.desc: Pinning a hidden item keeps it.
stack.hidden.title: Hidden items
stack.hidden.desc: A hidden item shows as dots with a lock and is not searchable. Press Return or click it to reveal it, and again to paste. It is never given to AI assistants.
fault.board_empty: Type a name for the board.
fault.board_bad_chars: That name has characters that cannot be used.
fault.board_reserved: That name belongs to a filter. Pick another.
fault.board_taken: A board with that name already exists.
fault.board_full: The limit of boards is reached.
mascot.enable.title: Clipboard mascot
mascot.enable.desc: A small pixel character comes out of the notch to fetch what you copy, brings the files you add from Finder, and sees files off when you drag them out of the shelf. It carries a stand-in, never what you copied. Nothing moves while Reduce motion is on.
mascot.character.title: Character
mascot.character.desc: Each one reaches in its own way: silk, a tongue, a beam, a wisp, a spell or a bolt. Point at the picture to see it pleased.
mascot.farewell.title: When a file leaves the shelf
mascot.farewell.desc: Guard: it escorts the file to where you drop it and salutes. Miss: it holds on until the file is gone, then waves goodbye.
mascot.try.title: Try it
mascot.try.desc: Plays a copy toward the pointer, even while the mascot is off.
mascot.aim.title: Where it aims
mascot.aim.on: At the selected text, in the apps that tell where it is, and otherwise at the pointer.
mascot.aim.off: At the pointer. With Accessibility allowed (General page) it aims at the selected text in the apps that tell where it is.
mascot.finder.title: Add files from Finder
mascot.finder.desc: Right-click files in Finder and choose Add to Figghost Shelf, under Services or Quick Actions. This works with the mascot off too.
page.wheel.sub: Drag files from Finder, tap a key, and drop them on a slot to convert, compress or send them.
wheel.enable.title: Use the drag wheel
wheel.enable.desc: While you drag files or folders, tapping a key opens a wheel of slots around the pointer. Drop the files on a slot to run it. The wheel stays open until you let go of the mouse button; dropping in the middle or outside the wheel does nothing. Everything runs on this Mac, and the new files are written next to the originals, which are never changed.
wheel.formats.title: Convert formats
wheel.formats.desc: Convert the files to another format: images, video, audio, PDF and documents, and any file or folder to ZIP, TAR or TGZ.
wheel.tools.title: Tools
wheel.tools.desc: Make images, video and audio smaller, remove metadata, cut out a background, copy the text in an image, annotate it, and merge or split PDFs.
wheel.actions.title: Actions
wheel.actions.desc: Copy the path or the files, send with AirDrop, open Terminal in the folder, show in Finder, or put the files on the shelf.
wheel.key.title: Key
wheel.key.desc: Tap this key, on its own, while dragging, or choose Other key and press any key you like. Two wheels that are on cannot share a key. Option on its own stays a plain copy drag unless a wheel uses it, and Escape always ends the drag.
wheel.slots.title: Slots
wheel.slots.desc: Choose which slots this wheel can show. A wheel shows only the slots that suit every file you drag. New slots in a later version show up here switched on.
fault.wheel_key_taken: Another wheel that is on already uses that key. Choose a different key first.
fault.wheel_failed: Could not watch the mouse for file drags.
page.mole.sub: The health of this Mac and what can be cleaned from it. Lists fill in by themselves; choose rows and remove them together.
mole.health.title: Health score
mole.free.title: What can be cleaned
mole.clean.title: Free up disk space
mole.clean.desc: App and browser caches, logs, developer caches and the Trash. They are emptied, not moved to the Trash; apps make them again when needed.
mole.clean.body: The contents of the chosen folders are deleted for good. Apps make their caches again when needed.
mole.purge.title: Build folders of projects
mole.purge.desc: node_modules, target, build, .venv, bin and obj and similar folders that their tools make again, found in the usual project folders.
mole.purge.body: The chosen build folders are deleted for good. Building the project makes them again.
mole.installers.title: Old installer files
mole.installers.desc: .dmg, .pkg, .iso and .xip files in Downloads, Desktop and Documents.
mole.installers.body: The chosen files go to the Trash, where they can be put back.
mole.apps.title: Apps with their leftovers
mole.apps.desc: Each app and what it left in Library go to the Trash together, so they can be put back. Quit an app before removing it.
mole.apps.body: The chosen apps and their leftover files go to the Trash.
mole.docker.title: Docker resources
mole.docker.desc: What Docker keeps: containers with their logs, images, volumes, networks and the build cache.
mole.docker.down: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop and refresh.
mole.docker.disk: Docker Desktop takes {size} on this Mac.
mole.docker.clear_logs.body: The logs of every container are emptied for good. The containers keep running.
mole.docker.unused.body: Stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images and dangling build cache are removed. Volumes are kept.
mole.docker.cache.body: All build cache that nothing uses is removed. The next build takes longer.
mole.docker.rm.body: The chosen containers are removed, running ones are stopped first. Their volumes are kept.
mole.docker.logs.body: The logs of the chosen containers are emptied for good.
mole.docker.rmi.body: The chosen images are removed. An image a container uses cannot be removed.
mole.docker.volume_rm.body: The chosen volumes and the data in them are deleted for good. A volume in use cannot be removed.
mole.docker.network_rm.body: The chosen networks are removed. A network in use cannot be removed.
mole.procs.title: Programs left running
mole.procs.desc: Servers and browsers that a coding agent started and that outlived it: their parent is gone, they are over ten minutes old, and they are of a known kind. Nothing is stopped by itself. The size is the memory each takes.
mole.procs.stop.body: The chosen programs are asked to end, and made to if they do not, with the programs they started. Anything they had not saved is lost.
mole.procs.done.partial: Stopped {n} programs, {failed} could not be stopped.
mole.docker_containers.title: Containers
mole.docker_containers.desc: Start, stop, restart, clear the logs of or remove the chosen containers.
mole.docker_images.title: Images
mole.docker_images.desc: The size is what removing an image frees: the layers no other image shares.
mole.docker_volumes.title: Volumes
mole.docker_volumes.desc: Volumes hold data; removing one deletes it.
mole.docker_networks.title: Networks
mole.docker_networks.desc: Networks made by you or by Compose. The built-in ones are not listed.
mole.analyze.title: What takes the space
mole.analyze.desc: The biggest entries first. Open a folder to look inside it; what is chosen goes to the Trash.
mole.analyze.body: The chosen files and folders go to the Trash, where they can be put back.
mole.result.partial: Removed {n} items, {size} freed. {failed} could not be removed.
page.islands.sub: Small notices that come out of the closed notch for a moment: Caps Lock, the charger, a full or low battery, a drive, a finished download, a camera or microphone in use.
islands.enable.title: Show live islands
islands.enable.desc: Nothing here reads what is on the screen or what is typed. Each notice can be switched off below.
islands.caps.title: Caps Lock
islands.caps.desc: A notice each time it turns on or off.
islands.power.title: Power and battery
islands.power.desc: When the charger is plugged in or out, and when the battery is full or low.
islands.drives.title: Drives
islands.drives.desc: When a drive arrives or leaves. A drive that is plugged in can be ejected from the menu bar panel.
islands.downloads.title: Finished downloads
islands.downloads.desc: When a file in the Downloads folder has stopped growing. Only names and sizes are looked at.
islands.camera.title: Camera
islands.camera.desc: Stays on the notch while an app is using the camera. It says that it is in use, not which app.
islands.microphone.title: Microphone
islands.microphone.desc: Stays on the notch while an app is using the microphone. It says that it is in use, not which app.
islands.full.title: Full at
islands.full.desc: Say the battery is full when it reaches this charge while plugged in.
islands.low.title: Low at
islands.low.desc: Say the battery is low when it falls to this charge on battery.
islands.nobattery: This Mac has no battery, so the notices about it never appear.
islands.seconds.title: How long a notice stays
islands.seconds.desc: The camera and microphone notices stay as long as they are in use.
page.utilities.sub: Keep the Mac awake, mute the microphone for every app at once, lock the keyboard while you wipe it, snooze the notch, switch to the dark appearance, hide the desktop icons, and copy the link of a browser tab.
util.enable.title: Use the utilities
util.enable.desc: Each has a place in the menu bar panel, a shortcut that works in any app, and a notice on the notch.
util.awake.now.title: Keep this Mac awake
util.awake.now.desc: Stops the Mac from sleeping on its own, as long as Figghost runs. Closing the lid still sleeps it.
util.awake.length.title: Length from the shortcut
util.awake.length.desc: How long it lasts when started with the shortcut or the button. The menu bar panel offers each length.
util.awake.display.title: Keep the screen lit too
util.awake.display.desc: Off lets the screen turn itself off while the Mac stays awake.
util.awake.shortcut.desc: Starts or stops it. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
util.mic.now.title: Mute the microphone
util.mic.now.desc: Mutes the microphone itself, so every meeting app hears nothing and none has a button to find.
util.snooze.now.title: Snooze the notch
util.snooze.now.desc: The notch stops opening when the pointer reaches the top of the screen, for when you present or play. A click on it, and anything that asks for you such as a coding agent that waits for an answer, still open it.
util.snooze.length.title: Length of a snooze
util.snooze.length.desc: How long it lasts when started with the shortcut or the button. The menu bar panel offers each length.
util.snooze.shortcut.desc: Starts or ends a snooze. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
util.lock.now.title: Lock the keyboard
util.lock.now.desc: Every key is ignored until the time is up, so you can wipe it without typing. Command and Escape unlock it at once. The pointer still works.
util.lock.seconds.title: Longest it stays locked
util.lock.seconds.desc: It unlocks by itself after this long.
util.lock.access.title: Accessibility
util.lock.access.desc: Needed to hold the keys back.
util.dark.title: Dark appearance
util.dark.desc: Switches the whole Mac between dark and light, as System Settings does.
util.desktop.title: Desktop icons
util.desktop.desc: Hides the files and drives on the desktop, for a clean screen to share. The Finder starts again to take it; its windows come back. Switching the utilities off shows them again.
util.automation.title: Automation
util.automation.desc: The appearance is changed through System Events and the link is read from the browser, so macOS asks once for each whether Figghost may control it. A refusal is changed here.
util.link.title: Copy the link of the tab in front
util.link.desc: Press the shortcut in Safari, Chrome, Edge, Brave or Vivaldi and the address of the tab in front is copied with its title. An incognito window gives nothing.
util.link.format.title: Written as
util.link.format.desc: Markdown suits notes, chats and code; the address alone suits everything else.
page.breaks.sub: Rest your eyes for a moment after a while at the Mac, and be reminded to blink and to sit up.
breaks.enable.title: Remind me to rest my eyes
breaks.enable.desc: Only time at the Mac counts. A break is announced on the notch ten seconds before it starts.
breaks.next.title: Next break
breaks.work.title: A break every
breaks.work.desc: Twenty minutes is the 20-20-20 rule: every twenty minutes, look twenty feet away for twenty seconds.
breaks.length.title: Each break lasts
breaks.length.desc: Five minutes is time to stand up and walk a little.
breaks.cover.title: Cover the screens
breaks.cover.desc: Blurs every display with a card to skip the break or have it five minutes later. Off, the break shows on the notch only.
breaks.sound.title: Sound
breaks.sound.desc: A soft sound when a break starts and ends.
breaks.shortcut.title: Shortcut
breaks.shortcut.desc: Starts a break now, or ends the one that runs. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
breaks.blink.title: Blink
breaks.blink.desc: A notice on the notch, for eyes that stare at a screen and forget to blink.
breaks.posture.title: Sit up
breaks.posture.desc: A notice on the notch to sit up straight and let the shoulders drop.
breaks.meetings.title: In a meeting
breaks.meetings.desc: A camera or a microphone is in use. The break comes as soon as the meeting ends.
breaks.fullscreen.title: An app is full screen
breaks.fullscreen.desc: A film, a game or a presentation fills the screen.
breaks.note.title: Away counts as a break.
breaks.note: Keyboard and pointer still for five minutes, or for a whole break if that is longer, start the count again. Reading or watching without touching still counts, since the eyes stay on the screen.
page.dictation.sub: Put the caret in a text box, press the shortcut and speak. The words go in when you stop.
dictation.enable.title: Speak instead of typing
dictation.enable.desc: A microphone comes to the middle of the screen and shows the words as they are understood. Return puts them in, Escape throws them away, the arrows change the language.
dictation.shortcut.title: Shortcut
dictation.shortcut.desc: Press it again to put the words in now.
dictation.language.title: Language spoken
dictation.language.desc: Each language has its own model, the one macOS keeps.
dictation.on_device.title: Only on this Mac
dictation.on_device.desc: The audio never leaves the Mac. Off, a language this Mac cannot recognize by itself is sent to Apple to be recognized.
dictation.silence_seconds.title: Put the words in after a silence of
dictation.silence_seconds.desc: Counted from the last word. With Never, the words go in only with Return or the shortcut.
dictation.sound.title: Sounds
dictation.sound.desc: A soft sound when the microphone opens and when the words go in.
dictation.speech.title: Speech Recognition
dictation.speech.desc: To turn the voice into words.
dictation.microphone.title: Microphone
dictation.microphone.desc: Only while the panel is open.
dictation.accessibility.title: Accessibility
dictation.accessibility.desc: To put the words into the text box. Without it they are left on the clipboard.
page.jarvis.sub: Press the shortcut, type a question and read the answer in a panel of Liquid Glass. Beta.
jarvis.enable.title: Ask Jarvis (Beta)
jarvis.enable.desc: A chat opens in the middle of the screen. Return sends your question, Escape stops the answer and then closes the panel. Turning it on sends what you type there to the service you choose below.
jarvis.shortcut.title: Shortcut
jarvis.shortcut.desc: Press it again to close the panel.
jarvis.provider.title: Service
jarvis.provider.desc: Who answers. Each needs its own key, except a model on this Mac.
jarvis.model.title: Model
jarvis.model.desc: Leave empty for the service's usual one. Names change, so type the one you want.
jarvis.key.title: Key
jarvis.key.desc: Kept in the Keychain of this Mac, never in the settings file.
jarvis.signin.expired: The sign-in ended, sign in again
jarvis.signin.note: Jarvis signs in to ChatGPT by itself, in your browser, and keeps the sign-in in the Keychain of this Mac; the Codex program is not needed. Questions count against your ChatGPT plan. This is not an official way for other programs to use that service, and OpenAI may stop it at any time.
jarvis.voice.title: Talk to Jarvis
jarvis.voice.desc: The panel asks what you want, listens, and sends what you said after a silence. Turn it off to only type.
jarvis.language.title: Language spoken
jarvis.language.desc: Each language has its own model, the one macOS keeps.
jarvis.on_device.title: Only on this Mac
jarvis.on_device.desc: The audio never leaves the Mac. Off, a language this Mac cannot recognize by itself is sent to Apple to be recognized.
jarvis.speak.title: Read the answer aloud
jarvis.speak.desc: Each sentence is read as soon as it is written, in the language it is in, with the voice of this Mac.
jarvis.sound.title: Sounds
jarvis.sound.desc: A soft sound when Jarvis wakes, answers, and when something goes wrong.
jarvis.speech.title: Speech Recognition
jarvis.speech.desc: To turn your voice into words.
jarvis.microphone.title: Microphone
page.network.sub: See which app uses which connection and how much, and wire an app to Wi-Fi, Ethernet or both.
network.enable.title: Watch the network
network.enable.desc: Reads what each app sends and receives, once a second and only while this page is open. Nothing leaves the Mac.
network.open.desc: Opens in a window of its own: each connection is a circle and each app a box you can move anywhere. Wire one connection to another to combine them.
network.apps.none: No app is using the network yet.
network.control.title: Apply the wires
network.control.desc: Points the proxy settings of macOS at Figghost, so each app that follows them (browsers and most apps) leaves by its wire, within its limit. Apps that ignore those settings, such as many games and command line tools, are only watched. macOS may ask for an administrator password. Turned off, every setting goes back as it was.
network.status.on: On: apps that follow the proxy settings go through Figghost
network.status.denied: The password was not given, so nothing changed. Turn the switch off and on to ask again.
network.status.failed: The settings of macOS could not be changed.
network.paused: A VPN carries everything, so every app takes the usual way and no wire is applied.
network.restore.desc: If websites stop opening after Figghost quit unexpectedly, this puts the settings of macOS back as they were.
network.hub.merge.desc: Every connection at once: each new connection of the app takes the next one
network.watching: Wires are kept now and take effect once Apply the wires is on in Settings. An app without a wire goes the way macOS chooses, drawn dashed.
network.drag: Drag from the ring of a connection to an app, or from the edge of an app to a connection. Wire Wi-Fi to Ethernet to combine them: an app wired to the big circle uses both, to a small one only that one. Drag the middle of a box or a circle to move it. Hold Space and drag to move around, hold Control and scroll to zoom.
network.arrange.name: By name
network.q.down: No answer from the internet through it
network.merge.resize: Drag to make the circle larger or smaller
network.card.held: Held to {speed} for the apps above it
network.metered.title: Save data on metered connections
network.metered.desc: On a connection you pay for by the byte, such as a phone's, only the apps you allow use it, and a cap can stop the rest. It applies to apps that follow the proxy settings, so Apply the wires must be on; other apps are only counted.
network.metered.auto.title: Take a phone's connection for metered
network.metered.auto.desc: A connection named iPhone or Android, or with the address a phone gives when it shares its data, counts as metered. It is a guess: mark a connection by hand under Connections to correct it.
network.metered.allow.title: Apps allowed on a metered connection
network.metered.allow.none: No app is allowed: every app that follows the proxy is held back.
network.metered.cap.title: Data cap
network.metered.cap.desc: What the metered connections may move in a period, counted by Figghost. At the cap every app that follows the proxy is refused until the period ends.
network.metered.period.title: Counted over
network.metered.now: On a metered connection now ({link}): only the allowed apps go on.
network.metered.not: Not on a metered connection now.
network.metered.cap.used: Used on metered connections this period: {used} of {cap}.
network.metered.cap.over: The cap is reached: every app that follows the proxy is refused.
network.card.hosts: Sites and addresses it talks to
network.card.hosts.none: Nothing seen yet. Apps that follow the proxy show the site name, the others show the address.
network.card.block.note: Blocked: every connection this app opens through the proxy is refused.
network.anomaly.title: Tell me when an app uploads a lot
network.anomaly.desc: The notch says so when an app sends in five minutes more than 50 MB and more than ten times what it usually sends in an hour. Needs a day of history for the app, which Figghost counts for it.
network.anomaly.ignore.title: Apps never reported
network.anomaly.ignore.desc: A backup or a sync is meant to send a lot.
network.watch.title: Tell me when the internet goes away
network.watch.desc: The notch says so when the internet is lost, when it is back, and when a network such as a hotel's asks you to sign in. Every five seconds it opens one small connection and, once, asks Apple's page for such checks. Works with the rest of this page off.
network.login.title: Open the sign-in page
network.login.desc: Opens the page a network that asks for a login shows in the browser.
network.dns.title: Encrypt the names this Mac looks up
network.dns.desc: Websites and apps ask a DNS server for the address of every name, and anyone on the way can read those questions. This makes a profile that sends them encrypted (DNS over HTTPS) to the server you choose. macOS asks you to approve it in System Settings, General, Device Management, and you can remove it there at any time.
network.dns.nextdns.hint: The six letters and digits of your configuration, such as a1b2c3
network.dns.warn: On a company network or a VPN that has its own names, an outside server cannot look them up: remove the profile if work sites stop opening. Phone sharing asks the DNS of the Mac, so stop and start it again after changing this.
network.links.desc: Each connection of this Mac, how well it answers, whether the web and secure sites open through it, and a test of its speed. A test takes a few seconds and moves up to 40 MB down and 12 MB up through that connection alone, so on a phone or a metered network leave it alone.
network.speed.done.noup: Down {down}, upload could not be measured, {rtt} ms to connect
network.speed.plain: Measured without TLS, since secure sites do not open through this connection.
network.speed.failed.offline: Nothing gets through this connection to the internet.
network.speed.failed.login: This network asks for a sign-in before it lets anything through.
network.speed.failed.tls: Secure connections through it were refused for their certificate, and the speed could not be measured.
network.speed.failed.slow: It moved nothing in the time, so the speed could not be measured.
network.web.none: The web does not open through this connection.
network.web.login: This connection asks for a sign-in.
network.web.tls: Secure sites (HTTPS) fail the certificate check here: the network may be opening secure traffic and signing it again with a certificate this Mac does not trust.
network.web.fail: Secure sites (HTTPS) do not open through this connection.
network.wifi.line: {standard}, channel {channel} ({band} GHz, {width} MHz), signal {rssi} dBm, noise {noise} dBm, link {rate} Mbps
network.history.title: Keep the history
network.history.desc: Adds up what each app sends and receives, by connection, for 90 days, also while this page is closed. Only the name of the app and the bytes are kept, on this Mac. An app that opens and closes a connection between two looks may be missed in part.
network.history.pace.title: Look every
network.history.pace.desc: Shorter is more exact and costs a little more. While this page is open it looks every second anyway.
network.history.none: Nothing counted yet. Leave Keep the history on for a few minutes.
network.history.export.title: Export
network.history.export.desc: Writes a file into Downloads and shows it in Finder: one line for each day or month, app and connection.
network.tether.title: Phone sharing
network.tether.desc: An Android phone on a USB cable uses this Mac's connection. Its Wi-Fi and mobile data can stay off.
network.tether.missing: Phone sharing needs two free tools, installed once. Paste this in Terminal:
network.tether.none.hint: Plug in an Android phone with USB debugging on (Settings, Developer options).
network.tether.unauthorized.hint: Unlock the phone and allow this Mac on its screen.
network.tether.ready.hint: The phone asks once to allow a VPN connection: that is how it takes this Mac's connection.
network.tether.running.hint: The phone is on this Mac's connection. Stop turns its VPN off too.
network.tether.lost.hint: The phone was unplugged. Plug it in again to go on, or stop.
network.tether.test.good: The phone reaches the internet and looks names up: {ms} ms.
network.tether.test.slow: The phone reaches the internet, but slowly: {ms} ms.
network.tether.test.dns: The phone reaches the internet by address, but cannot look names up. Stop and start sharing again, so that it asks the DNS of this Mac.
network.tether.test.none: The phone does not reach the internet. Check that it allowed the VPN, or unplug and plug it in again.
network.tether.test.untested: This phone has no tool to run the test. Open a website on it to check.
network.tether.apps: The phone asks this Mac's DNS servers, so names resolve as they do here. A few apps only trust Wi-Fi or mobile data and may still say there is no connection.
network.tether.iphone: An iPhone cannot take a Mac's connection over USB this way. Use Internet Sharing in System Settings, General, Sharing.
page.browser.sub: Block distracting sites while you focus, and send a video from the browser to Figghost.
browser.enable.title: Use Figghost Companion
browser.enable.desc: An extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi and Arc that talks only to Figghost on this Mac. It reads no page and asks for no access to any site.
browser.folder.title: 1. Load the extension
browser.folder.desc: Writes the extension into a folder and shows it in the Finder. In the browser, open the page of extensions, turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked and pick that folder.
browser.bridge.title: 2. Connect it to Figghost
browser.bridge.desc: For each browser you loaded it in: a small file in that browser's folder that names Figghost as the extension's bridge.
browser.none: No browser built on Chromium was found on this Mac.
browser.remove.title: Remove from this Mac
browser.remove.desc: Takes the bridge away from every browser and deletes the folder of the extension, even with the feature off. The extension loaded in a browser is removed on that browser's page of extensions.
browser.link.title: Extension
browser.block.title: Block these sites during Pomodoro work
browser.block.desc: While a work stage of Pomodoro runs, the sites below and their subdomains do not open in the browser. They open again when it ends.
browser.sites.title: Sites
browser.sites.desc: One a line. An address works too; only its site is kept.
browser.speed.title: Set the speed of videos
browser.speed.desc: The extension sets the video that plays in the browser to the speed below, for a lecture or a tutorial. The first time, right-click the extension's button in the browser and choose Allow Figghost to change the speed of videos: the browser asks once for access to pages. Nothing is read from them.
browser.download.title: Download with Figghost
browser.download.desc: The extension's button and the menu of a page or a link send it to Video download. Video download must be on, with yt-dlp installed.
page.notes.sub: Jot something down in a tab of the notch, and find it again as a plain text file.
notes.enable.title: Show the Notes tab
notes.enable.desc: Each note is a text file in a folder of its own, so any app can open it. What you type is saved a moment after you stop, and a deleted note goes to the Trash.
notes.size.title: Text size
notes.size.desc: How large the letters are in the editor.
notes.new.title: Start a blank note each time
notes.new.desc: The tab opens on an empty note, ready for quick capture, instead of the last one you wrote.
notes.folder.title: Notes folder
notes.folder.desc: {count} notes. Move, back up or sync the folder like any other.
page.launcher.sub: Pin apps, folders, files, websites and Shortcuts in groups, and open them with one press from the notch or a dock at the edge of the screen.
launcher.enable.title: Show the Launcher tab
launcher.enable.desc: A tile does something only when you press it. An app is found where it is now, a folder or a file opens as the Finder would, a website in your browser, and a Shortcut is run by its name. Swipe with two fingers or use the arrow keys to move between groups.
launcher.group.title: Group
launcher.group.desc: Each group holds up to twelve tiles, and there can be eight groups.
launcher.group.name: Name of the group
launcher.group.ph: A name, or empty for its number
launcher.group.confirm.body: Its tiles are unpinned. The apps, folders and files themselves are not touched.
launcher.none: Nothing is pinned in this group yet.
launcher.add.title: Add
launcher.add.desc: To the group chosen above. Right-click a folder tile to see what is in it.
launcher.url.title: Website
launcher.url.desc: An address of the web, or an email address. Other kinds of links are not pinned.
launcher.url.label: Address to pin
launcher.shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
launcher.shortcuts.desc: Runs a Shortcut of the Shortcuts app by its name. Your Shortcuts are read only when you ask.
launcher.shortcuts.none: No Shortcuts were found. Make one in the Shortcuts app first.
launcher.shortcuts.slow: The Shortcuts app did not answer in time. Try again in a moment.
sec.launcher.dock: Dock at the edge of the screen
launcher.dock.title: Show the dock
launcher.dock.desc: The same groups on glass at an edge of a screen, above your windows. It never takes the keyboard from the app you are using. Off by default; turning it off takes it away.
launcher.dock_edge.title: Edge
launcher.dock_edge.desc: The top belongs to the menu bar and the notch.
launcher.dock_display.title: Screen
launcher.dock_display.desc: When this screen is not connected, the dock goes to the main one, and back when it returns.
launcher.dock_group.title: Group shown first
launcher.dock_group.desc: Swipe with two fingers over the dock to move between groups.
launcher.dock_autohide.title: Hide until the pointer reaches the edge
launcher.dock_autohide.desc: The dock waits off the screen and comes out when the pointer touches the edge beside it.
fault.launcher_full: Twelve tiles is all that fit in a group. Remove one first, or use another group.
fault.launcher_already: That is pinned in this group already.
fault.launcher_groups_full: Eight groups is the most there can be.
page.weather.sub: See the weather of your cities in a tab of the notch, one at a time, now and for the next days.
weather.enable.title: Show the Weather tab
weather.enable.desc: The only tab that goes online. It asks Open-Meteo, which needs no account, only while the tab is open, only for the city it shows, and no more than once in ten minutes.
weather.city.title: Search for a city
weather.city.desc: Only the name you search for, and then the coordinates of the cities you add, are sent. The location of this Mac is never asked for.
weather.city.label: City name
weather.none: No city found with that name.
weather.problem.offline: No connection. Try again when you are online.
weather.problem.service: The weather service did not answer. Try again in a little while.
weather.places.desc: The tab opens on the first city. Flip through them with the arrows on the tab or the Left and Right keys.
weather.places.none: No city yet. Search for one above and press Add.
fault.weather_full: Eight cities is the most. Remove one first.
fault.weather_twice: That city is in the list already.
weather.units.title: Units
weather.units.desc: Degrees and the speed of the wind.
weather.sound.title: Weather sounds
weather.sound.desc: Rain, wind and thunder play softly behind the tab while it is open, matching the weather. Off by default.
page.prs.sub: See the review requests that wait for you on GitHub and GitLab.
prs.enable.title: Show the Pull requests tab
prs.enable.desc: The requests newest first, with a dot on the tab while there are some. Press one to open it in the browser. Figghost never sees your password or token: it asks the gh and glab tools you signed in with, and keeps nothing on disk.
prs.github.title: GitHub
prs.github.desc: Pull requests where your review is requested, through the gh tool.
prs.gitlab.title: GitLab
prs.gitlab.desc: Merge requests where your review is requested, through the glab tool.
prs.drafts.title: Include drafts
prs.drafts.desc: A draft is not ready for review yet, so it is left out unless you ask.
prs.minutes.title: Look again every
prs.minutes.desc: While this is on, the tools are asked this often, so that the dot on the tab is right.
page.updates.sub: See what has a newer version on this Mac and update it from the notch.
updates.enable.title: Show the Updates tab
updates.enable.desc: Homebrew formulae and casks, global npm packages, App Store apps (with the mas tool), Apple software updates, and the coding agents that update themselves: Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Droid and Amp. The version now is red and the new one green; tick rows to update them, or update all. Looks again every six hours.
updates.daily.title: Update everything every day
updates.daily.desc: Once a day, everything except Apple's updates is updated without asking. Apple's updates need an administrator, so they open System Settings when you update them yourself.
updates.off: Turn on the tab to look for updates.
page.pomodoro.sub: Work in sessions with breaks between them, and watch the time in the notch.
pomodoro.enable.title: Show the Pomodoro tab
pomodoro.enable.desc: Work sessions and breaks one after the other, a ring that fills as a stage passes, and the countdown in the closed notch while it runs. It is a tab beside Focus, which stays a plain countdown.
pomodoro.work.title: Work session
pomodoro.short.title: Short break
pomodoro.long.title: Long break
pomodoro.long.desc: The longer rest that ends a round.
pomodoro.rounds.title: Sessions in a round
pomodoro.rounds.desc: How many work sessions come before the long break.
pomodoro.auto.title: Start the next stage by itself
pomodoro.auto.desc: Off waits for you to press Start after each stage.
pomodoro.sound.title: Play a sound
pomodoro.sound.desc: A different one for the end of a session and the end of a break.
pomodoro.open.title: Open the notch on this tab
pomodoro.open.desc: It goes away again after a few seconds if the pointer is not on it.
pomodoro.closed.title: Show the countdown in the closed notch
pomodoro.closed.desc: While a stage runs, the time left sits beside the cutout. A click on it opens this tab.
pomodoro.shortcut.title: Shortcut
pomodoro.shortcut.desc: Starts, pauses and resumes from any app. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
pomodoro.stats.title: Sessions done
pomodoro.stats.desc: {today} today. {streak} days in a row. {days} days kept.
page.screentime.sub: See which apps had your time today and this week, in a tab of the notch.
screentime.enable.title: Count the time of each app
screentime.enable.desc: Every few seconds the app in front is given that time while you are at the Mac. Only the name of the app and the time are kept, on this Mac, for thirty days. No window title, text, screen or key is looked at, and it needs no permission. Sites are counted only when the switch below is on.
screentime.idle.title: Stop counting when I am away
screentime.idle.desc: Time stops counting once the keyboard and pointer have been still this long.
screentime.sites.title: Count by site too
screentime.sites.desc: When Safari or a browser built on Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi) is in front, the site of its front tab is given the time too, and the tab of the notch lists the sites. Only the name of the site is kept, such as github.com. Incognito windows are left out, but Safari does not say which of its windows are private, so those count. macOS asks once for each browser whether Figghost may read its tab. Firefox cannot be asked. Switching this off forgets the sites counted.
screentime.data.title: Counted so far
page.dayprogress.sub: See how much of the day has gone, with today's events along the line, in a tab of the notch.
dayprogress.enable.title: Show the day as a line
dayprogress.enable.desc: The tab shows the share of the day that has gone, a line from the morning to bedtime with today's events laid along it, and what is on now and what comes next. It reads the same calendars as the Calendar tab and nothing else; if the calendar is not allowed yet, allow it under Notch tabs, Calendar.
dayprogress.wake.title: The day begins at
dayprogress.wake.desc: The left end of the line, where 0% is.
dayprogress.bed.title: The day ends at
dayprogress.bed.desc: The right end of the line, where 100% is.
dayprogress.reminders.title: Mark reminders on the line
dayprogress.reminders.desc: A reminder due today at a time is marked as a dot on the line, and those still to do are counted under it. It needs the Reminders access that is given under Notch tabs, Calendar.
page.devices.sub: See the charge of your Bluetooth mouse, keyboard and headphones in a tab of the notch.
devices.enable.title: Show the charge of connected devices
devices.enable.desc: The tab lists the Bluetooth devices that are connected, each with the charge it reports, and marks one that is running low. The system is asked when the tab opens and every half minute while it shows, and never otherwise. A device that does not report its charge to the Mac is listed without one. It needs no permission and nothing is stored.
devices.low.title: Call a device low at
devices.low.desc: A device at or under this charge gets a warning colour and the word Low. A pair of earbuds counts each bud, not the case.
