page.displays.sub: Set the brightness and contrast of an external display from a tab of the notch, as its own buttons would, the color profile of any display, and where the displays are.
displays.enable.title: Show the Displays tab
displays.enable.desc: Each external display that answers over DDC/CI gets a card with a slider for its brightness and one for its contrast, and the display itself changes, not a filter over the picture. The displays are looked for when the tab opens. It needs no permission. A display behind a hub, a DisplayLink adapter or some HDMI ports does not answer.
displays.profiles.title: Choose the color profile of each display
displays.profiles.desc: Every display gets a card, the built-in one too, with a menu of its own profile and the ones macOS comes with: Display P3, sRGB, Adobe RGB, Rec. 709, Rec. 2020 and the others System Settings lists under Displays. The choice is the same as there, for this user, and the picture changes at once; choosing the display's own profile puts it back.
displays.arrange.title: Arrange the displays from the tab
displays.arrange.desc: With more than one display connected, the tab has a second view, Arrange, with the displays drawn where they are, as in System Settings. Drag a display to move it and it goes flush against the nearest side of another; drag the white bar onto another display to make it the main one, with the menu bar and the Dock. Its menu chooses what the display is used as: the main display, an extended display, or a mirror of another. The change is kept, as System Settings keeps it.
displays.keys.title: Brightness keys set the external displays
displays.keys.desc: The brightness keys move every external display together and show the level in the look of the volume indicator; Shift and Option together take a smaller step. While a built-in screen is lit the keys stay with it, and Control with a key sets the external displays. Needs Accessibility.
page.present.sub: Show a display, an area, a window or an app to an audience on another display, with a zoom that follows your pointer.
present.enable.title: Show the Present tab
present.enable.desc: Choose on the tab what to present and where, and start: the audience sees it full screen on the other display, a projector or a TV, or in a window of its own that a video call can share, while the rest of your screen stays yours. The notch and every other window of Figghost are never in the picture; a notification that appears on a display that is shown is, so turn on Do Not Disturb before a talk.
present.access.title: Screen Recording
present.access.no: Not allowed yet: the picture cannot be shown without it.
present.source.title: What the tab offers first
present.source.desc: A display shows all of it; an area is dragged out on the frozen screen; a window is shown on its own even while other windows cover it; an app shows all its windows on its display and nothing else.
present.fps.title: Frames a second
present.fps.desc: 60 for video and smooth scrolling, 30 to spare the battery on slides.
present.cursor.title: Show the pointer
present.cursor.desc: The pointer is in the picture, where it is on your screen.
present.border.title: Frame what is shown
present.border.desc: A thin green frame on your screen around the area or display the audience sees. The audience does not see it.
present.auto.title: Zoom in where you click
present.auto.desc: A click zooms the audience's picture in on it, the view follows the pointer once it nears an edge, and after a quiet moment it goes back to the whole picture, as screen recorders that zoom by themselves do. The zoom keys step in and out around the pointer at any time.
present.zoom.title: Zoom of a click
present.zoom.desc: How large a click makes the picture.
present.zoomout.title: Back to the whole picture after
present.zoomout.desc: Seconds without a click. Typing does not count, so choose longer for live demos.
present.ring.title: Ring the pointer from the start
present.ring.desc: A yellow ring that the audience can follow, as a laser pointer is. It can also be turned on and off while presenting.
present.clicks.title: Show clicks
present.clicks.desc: A ripple where the mouse is clicked.
present.spot.title: Size of the spotlight
present.spot.desc: The spotlight darkens all but a circle around the pointer. It is turned on while presenting, from the tab or with its key.
present.closed.title: Show the time in the closed notch
present.closed.desc: While presenting, how long it has run sits beside the cutout, green while the audience sees the picture live and orange while it is held or covered. A click on it opens the tab.
present.keys.desc: The key that starts works in any app while the feature is on. The others work only while a presentation runs, so they take no key from your apps the rest of the time. The letters follow the slide shows where they can: B and W for a black and a white screen as in PowerPoint and Keynote, Z for zoom as in ZoomIt and the macOS zoom. Press Delete while recording to turn one off.
present.key.start.desc: Starts with what the tab chose, or stops.
present.key.zoom_in.desc: One step closer, around the pointer: 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6 and 8 times.
present.key.zoom_reset.desc: Back to all of it at once.
present.key.auto: Zoom in where you click, on or off
present.key.spotlight.desc: Darkens all but a circle around the pointer.
present.key.freeze.desc: The audience keeps seeing the last picture while you look something up; press again to go live.
present.key.black.desc: As B in a slide show; press again to come back.
present.key.white.desc: As W in a slide show.
page.notifications.sub: Receive the notifications of your apps on the notch, or keep them in the system and find them on a tab of the notch.
notifications.enable.title: Show notifications on the notch
notifications.enable.desc: The notifications your apps send are read from Notification Center as they come and listed on a Notifications tab, newest first; a click on one opens its app.
notifications.access.title: Full Disk Access
notifications.access.no: Not allowed yet. macOS keeps notifications where only an app with Full Disk Access may read them: turn Figghost on in the list, then quit and open it again.
notifications.access.unknown: Checked once the feature is on: macOS keeps notifications where only an app with Full Disk Access may read them, and the button opens that list.
notifications.mode.title: Receive notifications
notifications.mode.desc: Through the system: macOS shows its banners as before, and the tab keeps the list. Through the notch: each one comes out of the closed notch at once, ahead of the music and the date and time, with the app's icon, its title and its words.
notifications.banners.title: Turn off macOS's banners
notifications.banners.desc: So that a notification does not show twice: in System Settings, Notifications, set the alert style of each app whose notifications should come through the notch to None. They still reach Notification Center, and so the notch. Do Not Disturb does the same for every app at once.
notifications.seconds.title: Time on the notch
notifications.seconds.desc: How long a notification stays on the closed notch; a newer one takes its place.
notifications.badge.title: Count the unread
notifications.badge.desc: A red number beside the closed notch shows how many came since you last looked at this tab. Opening the tab clears it.
notifications.preview.title: Show what they say
notifications.preview.desc: Off shows only the app and New notification, for a notch that others can see.
notifications.privacy.title: Read, never written or sent
notifications.privacy.desc: Figghost only reads the store macOS keeps, and only when it changes. Nothing is written to it, nothing is kept on disk and nothing leaves this Mac; the list goes when Figghost quits.
page.outlook.sub: New mail and calendar reminders of Outlook on a tab of the notch, and a card to read one at a glance.
outlook.enable.title: Outlook on the notch
outlook.enable.desc: The notifications the Outlook app sends are listed on an Outlook tab, newest first; a click on one opens it in a card in the middle of the screen. No account is signed in: the sender, the subject and the first lines are what Outlook puts in its notification.
outlook.access.title: Full Disk Access
outlook.access.ok: Allowed: Outlook's notifications can be read.
outlook.access.no: Not allowed yet: turn Figghost on in the list, then quit and open it again.
outlook.access.unknown: Checked once the feature is on: macOS keeps notifications where only an app with Full Disk Access may read them.
outlook.access.missing: The Outlook app is not on this Mac.
outlook.notch.title: Show on the notch
outlook.notch.desc: A new mail comes out of the closed notch for a few seconds, with the sender and the subject.
outlook.seconds.title: Time on the notch
outlook.preview.title: Show what it says
outlook.preview.desc: Off shows only New mail on the notch, for a notch that others can see.
outlook.drop.title: Drop from the notch
outlook.drop.desc: A new mail falls from the notch as a drop to the middle of the screen and opens into the card to read it. A press anywhere else or Escape puts it away.
outlook.events.title: Calendar reminders
outlook.events.desc: The reminders of meetings and events that Outlook sends are listed and announced as well, under Calendar.
outlook.banners.title: Turn off Outlook's banners
outlook.banners.desc: So that a mail does not show twice: in System Settings, Notifications, Microsoft Outlook, set the alert style to None. Its notifications still reach Notification Center, and so this tab.
outlook.privacy.title: Read, never written or sent
outlook.privacy.desc: Figghost only reads the notifications macOS keeps. Nothing is written, nothing is kept on disk and nothing leaves this Mac; the list goes when Figghost quits.
page.video.sub: Play a live stream or a video in a tab of the notch.
video.enable.title: Show the Video tab
video.enable.desc: Beta. Plays the address below in the open notch, without sound. It plays only while the tab shows, so a closed notch fetches nothing. HLS (.m3u8), MP4 and MOV over https, or a local file, are the kinds macOS plays.
video.url.title: Address
video.url.desc: An https address, or file:// for a video on this Mac. Press Enter to save it.
page.system.sub: See the processor, memory, network and disk at work in a tab of the notch.
system.enable.title: Show the System tab
system.enable.desc: The tab reads the Mac only while it is open and nothing runs when it is closed. It needs no permission.
system.processor.title: Processor
system.processor.desc: The load of each core, with the efficiency cores apart from the performance ones.
system.memory.title: Memory
system.memory.desc: What apps hold, what is wired and what is compressed, with the pressure and the swap.
system.network.title: Network
system.network.desc: Speed down and up, and the last readings drawn as a line.
system.details.title: Graphics, disk, heat, fans and battery
system.details.desc: A row of small figures: the heat of the processor in degrees, and the speed of the fans. The fans and the battery are there only on a Mac that has them.
system.bar.processor.title: Processor load
system.bar.processor.desc: The load of all the cores together, as a percentage.
system.bar.memory.title: Memory in use
system.bar.memory.desc: What apps, the system and compression hold, as a share of all the memory.
system.bar.network.title: Network speed
system.bar.network.desc: Down and up together as text, or up over down.
system.bar.gpu.title: Graphics load
system.bar.gpu.desc: How busy the graphics processor is, as a percentage.
system.bar.heat.title: Processor heat
system.bar.heat.desc: In degrees, on a Mac that reports it.
system.bar.disk.title: Startup disk
system.bar.disk.desc: The room left on the startup disk.
system.bar.combined.title: One item for all
system.bar.combined.desc: Off, each figure is an item of its own that Command-drag moves.
system.bar.color.title: Graphs in colour
system.bar.color.desc: Lines and cores in the accent colour, a core above 85% in red. Off, they take the colour of the menu bar.
system.bar.note.title: Read all the time.
system.bar.note: The figures you choose stay in the menu bar and are read as often as the tab, even while it is closed. A click on them opens the tab.
system.seconds.title: How often
system.seconds.desc: A short wait follows a spike closely and a long one reads less.
page.typing.sub: Type Vietnamese in every app with Telex or VNI, with no other input method. English words you type come back by themselves.
typing.enable.title: Type Vietnamese
typing.enable.desc: The marks go where they belong as you type. Needs Accessibility, like scrolling and window snapping.
typing.now.title: Typing in
typing.now.desc: The shortcut, the menu bar panel and this button switch between Vietnamese and English.
typing.notch.title: Language on the notch
typing.notch.desc: VI or EN stays on the closed notch while typing runs, under anything else that is live.
typing.tray.title: Language in the menu bar
typing.tray.desc: A small VI or EN beside the ghost. Click it to switch.
typing.flag.title: Flag instead of VI or EN
typing.flag.desc: The flag of Vietnam or of the United States stands for the language on the notch and in the menu bar.
typing.waving.title: Waving flag for Vietnamese
typing.waving.desc: The red flag with the gold star waves on the notch each time typing switches to Vietnamese.
typing.other.title: {name} is running
typing.other.desc: Two input methods would put every mark twice, so Figghost leaves the keys alone while {name} runs. Quit one of the two.
typing.method.desc: Telex types the marks with letters (aa is â, s the acute accent); VNI with digits (a6 is â, 1 the acute accent).
typing.modern.title: Marks where the new rules put them
typing.modern.desc: hoà, khoẻ, thuỷ. Off writes hòa, khỏe, thủy.
typing.english.title: Give English words back
typing.english.desc: text, with or push typed with Telex come back as they were when the word ends, instead of tẽt, ưith or púh.
typing.shortcut.desc: Switches between Vietnamese and English in any app. Press Delete while recording to remove it.
typing.apps.title: Apps where every key is left alone
typing.apps.desc: Typing in these apps stays as it is. iPhone Mirroring and remote desktops are always left alone, since their keys go to another device.
typing.access.title: Accessibility
typing.access.desc: Needed to read the keys and type the marks.
typing.engine.title: The engine
typing.engine.desc: The marks are put by the engine of Gõ Nhanh (copyright 2025 Gõ Nhanh Contributors, BSD 3-Clause License), which Figghost uses unchanged. Its licence is on the About page.
page.snippets.sub: Type a short abbreviation in any app and it is replaced by the text you saved: an email reply, an address, a signature, a piece of code.
snippets.enable.title: Replace abbreviations
snippets.enable.desc: Works with Vietnamese typing on or off. Nothing is replaced in password fields, where macOS hides the keys from every app.
snippets.access.title: Accessibility
snippets.access.desc: Needed to read the keys and put the text in.
snippets.other.title: {name} is running
snippets.other.desc: Two input methods would both rewrite what you type, so Figghost leaves the keys alone while {name} runs. Quit one of the two.
snippets.abbr.hint: Begin it with a character like ; so ordinary words are never replaced by accident, for example ;sig or ;addr. It is replaced the moment its last key is typed.
snippets.text.ph: What the abbreviation turns into. Line breaks are kept.
snippets.none: No snippets yet. Add the first one above.
snippets.shadow: {abbr} is finished first, so this one can never be typed in full.
snippets.remove.title: Remove this snippet?
snippets.remove.body: The abbreviation {abbr} will stop being replaced.
snippets.how.type.title: Short text is typed
snippets.how.type.desc: A text of one short line is typed in place of the abbreviation, key by key, as fast as the app takes it.
snippets.how.paste.title: Long text and line breaks are pasted
snippets.how.paste.desc: Typing a line break would press Return, which sends a message in a chat app. So these are pasted: your clipboard is kept, the text goes on it for a moment, and your clipboard is put back right after. Figghost does not add the text to the clipboard history.
snippets.how.telex.title: Works with Telex and VNI
snippets.how.telex.desc: The abbreviation is read from the keys you press, so ;dd is found even though Telex shows it as ;đ. Keys are read by their place on a US keyboard, so an abbreviation may hold letters, digits and the punctuation of one.
snippets.how.stop.title: When it stops looking
snippets.how.stop.desc: A click, an arrow key, Return, Tab, a space, a shortcut with Command, Control or Option, or another app coming to the front starts the abbreviation again. Backspace takes the last key back.
fault.snippets_long: An abbreviation may have at most 32 characters.
fault.snippets_space: An abbreviation cannot contain spaces or line breaks.
fault.snippets_untypeable: Use only the letters, digits and punctuation that a US keyboard types.
fault.snippets_no_text: Type the text it should turn into.
fault.snippets_text_long: A snippet may have at most 20,000 characters.
fault.snippets_duplicate: Another snippet already uses that abbreviation.
fault.snippets_full: There can be at most 500 snippets.
page.download.sub: Paste a link to a video and save it to your Mac. The work is done by yt-dlp, which you install yourself.
download.enable.title: Download videos
download.enable.desc: Adds a Download video entry to the menu bar panel that takes the link you copied, and shows the progress on the closed notch. Figghost does not include yt-dlp; it uses your copy. Only save videos you have the right to keep.
download.ytdlp.title: yt-dlp
download.ytdlp.missing: Not installed. In Terminal, run: brew install yt-dlp
download.ffmpeg.title: ffmpeg
download.ffmpeg.found: Found. It joins video and sound, so above 1080p (VP9, AV1) and other formats work, and music only is saved as m4a.
download.ffmpeg.missing: Not installed. Figghost joins H.264 video and AAC sound itself, so YouTube works up to 1080p. ffmpeg is needed only above 1080p (VP9, AV1), for sites with formats Figghost cannot join, and to turn music into m4a. To get it, run: brew install ffmpeg
download.link.label: Link to the video
download.quality.title: Quality
download.quality.desc: The best the site has, or no taller than the height you choose. Music only saves the sound.
download.playlist.title: Whole playlist
download.playlist.desc: A link to a playlist saves all of it. Off saves only the video the link points at.
download.folder.title: Save to
download.net.title: Use every connection at once
download.net.desc: Beta. Fetches a video in pieces over several connections at once and spreads them over the connections of the Mac (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, a phone on USB with Personal Hotspot on), as net-merge does, so their speeds add up. No administrator password is needed and only the downloads of Figghost take part. The first connection of a download to each site takes the usual connection of the Mac, a connection that fails with a site is kept away from it for a while, and while a VPN carries everything nothing is merged.
download.net.one: One connection: a video still comes in several pieces at once. Plug in a phone by USB with Personal Hotspot on, or an Ethernet cable, to add another.
download.net.paused: A VPN carries all traffic, so nothing is merged: downloads go through it as before.
download.list.empty: Nothing downloaded yet. Paste a link above.
download.err.ffmpeg: This video needs ffmpeg: Figghost cannot join its formats itself. In Terminal, run: brew install ffmpeg
fault.download_missing: yt-dlp is not installed. In Terminal, run: brew install yt-dlp
fault.download_bad_url: That is not a link that starts with http:// or https://.
download.lanes.title: Lanes, a download manager
download.lanes.desc: Lanes, by the maker of Figghost, downloads any file over many connections at once and picks up where it stopped. Its extension takes over the downloads of Chrome, Edge and Brave and puts a button on the videos you watch, with a choice of resolution; YouTube goes through yt-dlp. Free and open source (MIT).
download.lanes.notch.title: Show Lanes downloads on the notch
download.lanes.notch.desc: While Lanes downloads, the closed notch shows its icon and the share done, then a short notice when a download finishes or fails. Figghost only reads the list Lanes keeps for its extension. It works with Download videos off.
